title: GraphQL extensions entries under credential-like names
summary: A GraphQL response or error whose extensions map has an entry named like a credential (token, apiKey, secret) with a string value.
rationale: The specification reserves the extensions member for implementers with no restriction on its contents, so an entry called token may hold a secret, a public identifier, an error code or a trace token, and nothing in the specification tells them apart. A name alone does not establish confidentiality, and a value is not shown to be a secret by being in a response. Without a documented value grammar or a provider statement for the entry, the expectation is not assertable.

expectation.rationale: Left unresolved. The cited text states that the contents of extensions are unrestricted and implementer-defined, which settles neither confidentiality nor value shape. A provider statement for a specific extension entry, or a maintainer policy decision, would settle it per entry. No fixture is authored: a value that would need a guessed shape is described, not exemplified.

sources.supports: The response extensions entry, and an error extensions entry, must be a map and are reserved for implementers, with no additional restrictions on their contents.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Research for #197 (parent #158). Origin of the inputs: evidence-derived and synthetic, not observed in a real incident or product; the request shapes follow the specification examples and the response texts are invented. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Needs a maintainer decision or a provider source per entry before any outcome is asserted.
